newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila stocks close weaker on U.S. rate fears.
newsitem.headline: Manila stocks close weaker on U.S. rate fears.

text.p: Manila shares closed weaker on Monday as investors stayed on the sidelines awaiting developments on U.S. interest rates, brokers said.

"There was supposed to be some momentum because of the rise in the Dow Jones index but the computer problems at the exchange also discouraged investors," said Bogart Cruz, trading manager at Asia Pacific Capital Equities & Securities Corp.
The index fell 3.74 points, or 0.12 percent, to 3,166.42.
Losers overcame gainers 61 to 33 with 78 issues unchanged.

"Investors including foreign ones remained hesitant as they wait for the U.S. to declare interest rates," said Rudsend Alpay, trader at Lippo Securities. He said investors have factored in elections in the Philippines' Mindanao.
Trading will continue to be listless for the rest of the week, the traders said.
The market's opening was delayed by technical problems and stock exchange officials decided to extend trading by one hour to 1.0 p.m. (0500 GMT)
